subject: Customer SecQ: data territory, retention & decommissioning (hosted API)
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@holloway.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Jordan Singh <jordan.singh@holloway.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: SecQ: data territory, retention & decommissioning (hosted API)

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. Our security team pulled together a short set of clarifying Qs focused on where data lives, how long it’s kept, and the mechanics for full decommissioning. We’re on a tight timeline for our procurement review; responses by EOD Wednesday would be great. Questions below:

1) For the hosted API, do you allow tenant data to remain in a specific geographic region (US only) and can you guarantee not to replicate outside that region?
2) What are the default retention windows for: (a) request/response payloads, (b) embeddings/representations, (c) logs and audit trails, and (d) backups/snapshots?
3) Is there an API or process to request immediate deletion of a tenant’s data (logical delete + scrub from backups)? What are typical timelines for completion?
4) Do caches or transient stores (e.g., KV cache, prefix cache) persist beyond the responding request? If so, what TTLs apply and can they be disabled?
5) What evidence do you provide on completion (cert, ticket, audit record)?

We’ve attached the form our GRC team expects, but a concise email answering the above is fine.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Security, Holloway AI
alex.mercer@holloway.ai

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@holloway.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SecQ: data territory, retention & decommissioning (hosted API)

Alex —

Appreciate the list. Below are concise answers and we’ve attached a short playbook and an erasure-cert template for formal requests. I’ve looped in Marissa (security operations) and Rishi (solutions engineering) for any technical deep-dive.

1) Data territory / region: Yes — for hosted API customers we support region-scoped tenancy. If you choose a US-only tenancy we route and store persistent customer data in our US regions only. We do not replicate tenant-persistent storage to EU/APAC unless you explicitly enable multi-region. Transient routing for failover may cross regions only for requests in active failover scenarios; we can enumerate policies in the contract.

2) Default retention windows (configurable at tenant level):
   - Request/response payloads: 30 days by default for troubleshooting and quality monitoring; option to set to 0 (no persistent storage) at signup.
   - Embeddings / model-derived artifacts: Not stored by default. If you opt-in for operational features (e.g., semantic search, embedding index, or supervised fine-tuning) we persist embeddings in a customer-scoped index. Default retention for persisted embeddings is 90 days unless otherwise contractually agreed.
   - Logs & audit trails: Control-plane audit logs retained 365 days (for enterprise tiers we can extend), request-level telemetry (token counts/latency/cost) retained 180 days.
   - Backups & snapshots: Encrypted metadata/config backups retained 90 days; full backups (where applicable) retained per contract — default 90 days.

3) Deletion / erasure process:
   - API: We provide a tenant erasure endpoint (POST /v1/tenants/{id}/erase) which triggers a coordinated erase workflow.
   - Timeline: Logical deletion starts within 24–72 hours. Background jobs purge primary stores within 72 hours; removal from backup snapshots is asynchronous and typically completed within 30 days (we mark backups for deletion and run lifecycle purge jobs). Full cryptographic destruction of any physical media follows cloud provider timelines; we provide date-stamped attestations when requested.
   - Note: If you have stricter requirements (e.g., immediate backup scrub), we’ll include accelerated retention/backup-flush clauses in the SOW.

4) Caches / transient stores:
   - Prefix/KV caches: Designed to be in-memory or in-region ephemeral stores. Default TTL is 5 minutes for prefix/KV cache entries; entries are evicted based on LRU and TTL. These caches do not persist to long-term storage.
   - Customer-configurable: You can disable persistent caching at tenant scope (recommended if you require minimal footprint).

5) Evidence on completion:
   - We provide an erasure certificate (attached template) and a ticket history with timestamps. For enterprise contracts, we’ll supply a signed attestation and a downloadable audit record (CSV/JSON) of scrub events.

Attachments included: redwood_data_retention_playbook.pdf (summary of flows) and erasure-cert-template.docx (formal attest template).

If you’d like, Rishi can provide a short network diagram of region routing and Marissa can outline the SOC/process controls that back the erase pipeline.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Singh <jordan.singh@holloway.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@holloway.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SecQ: data territory, retention & decommissioning (hosted API)

Thanks Karthik — couple quick clarifications for procurement:

- When you say "not stored by default" for embeddings, can you confirm whether transient operational buffers (used during similarity search ops) ever end up in persistent indexes automatically? We want to ensure that unless we explicitly opt-in, no embeddings are written to durable storage.
- For the erase API timeline: do you provide a human-readable certificate and an audit export (CSV) automatically, or is that produced on request and takes extra time? Procurement prefers auto-generated certificate + download link so we can tie it to our internal workflow.

Jordan Singh
Senior Procurement Manager, Holloway AI

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Singh <jordan.singh@holloway.ai>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@holloway.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-04T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SecQ: data territory, retention & decommissioning (hosted API)

Jordan —

Quick clarifications:

- Embeddings / operational buffers: If you do not opt in for embedding features, operational buffers used for similarity calculations are kept in ephemeral memory and are never promoted to the persistent index. We will annotate this in the SOW: "No automatic promotion of embeddings to durable storage without explicit tenant opt-in."

- Certificates & audit exports: The erase endpoint produces a ticket and a timestamped audit record immediately. For Enterprise plans we enable an automated certificate generation workflow: once the erase job completes, the system generates an erasure certificate (PDF) and an audit CSV/JSON export and pushes it to the tenant's secure drive link (the same S3-backed location used for logs) — this is available within the stated retention purge window (typically within 72 hours of job completion). For standard plans we produce the audit export on request (2–5 business days).

Next steps:
- If Holloway wants automated certs and a US-only tenancy, I’ll put together an amendment with accelerated backup purge language and automated certificate generation (adds to SLA). Marissa — can you prep the SOC/process addendum for the SOW? Rishi — can you share the small region-routing diagram for inclusion in the appendix?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if you want to walk through timelines.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
